title: Will the answers keep sharing one thing, whatever signs you choose?
description: {{NAME_1}} sorts smooth river pebbles into rows, then tries a game with plus and minus signs between four numbers that come one after another. Every answer seems to share one feature, and the video stops on whether that will always happen.
teaching_notes: One idea: a pattern that holds in every try still needs a reason before we trust it. Collect guesses about what the answers share and do not confirm any; the chapter settles it. Watch for students who say the pattern must hold because it held a few times.

video_script.why: Before any rule appears, the child meets the puzzle that drives the chapter: a pattern that keeps working and asks for a reason.
video_script.substitution: Picture four cards in a row with sign cards in the gaps, and many tries piling up.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_1}} sorting smooth river pebbles into rows, then trying a game with signs between four numbers in a row

maths_rules: The game: four numbers that come one after another, plus or minus signs in the three gaps, then work out the answer.
No numbers, answers or symbols are drawn; the cards stay blank and the answers stay hidden.
The shared feature of the answers is never said or shown; the open question is left for the chapter.
video_script.design: One idea: a pattern that keeps working asks for a reason. Assumes nothing. Wrong idea: none is broken. The pebbles and the row of cards stay to the end; no hard clear.
